BIST STOCK DAILY BRIEF | November 11, 2026

MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
RISK-ON: normal volatility at 32.9% and broad participation, with all 8/8 sectors positive over one week. The 1M sector picture is less uniform: six sectors remain negative.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Transportation leads at +18.20% on the week; PGSUS (1W: +19.89% | 1M: +8.04%) ABOVE TREND and THYAO (1W: +18.77% | 1M: +9.06%) ABOVE TREND confirm strength. Technology & Telecom (+12.44%) and Banking & Finance (+11.60%) follow, led by KONTR (1W: +32.84% | 1M: +31.53%) ABOVE TREND and GARAN (1W: +18.41% | 1M: +19.14%) ABOVE TREND.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Retail & Food (+2.67%) and Construction & REIT (+2.86%) are the weakest weekly sectors, with both still down over one month. SOKM (1W: -10.21% | 1M: -14.87%) BELOW TREND and TKFEN (1W: -2.66% | 1M: -24.03%) BELOW TREND mark the clearest pressure.

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
KONTR (1W: +32.84% | 1M: +31.53%) ABOVE TREND, PGSUS (1W: +19.89% | 1M: +8.04%) ABOVE TREND, THYAO (1W: +18.77% | 1M: +9.06%) ABOVE TREND, GARAN (1W: +18.41% | 1M: +19.14%) ABOVE TREND, and TRALT (1W: +17.87% | 1M: -4.73%) RECOVERY.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
SOKM (1W: -10.21% | 1M: -14.87%) BELOW TREND, TKFEN (1W: -2.66% | 1M: -24.03%) BELOW TREND, KRDMD (1W: -1.42% | 1M: -13.11%) BELOW TREND, TUPRS (1W: -1.41% | 1M: -15.30%) BELOW TREND, and ASELS (1W: -1.31% | 1M: -3.15%) BELOW TREND.

6. Momentum Stocks?
KONTR (1W: +32.84% | 1M: +31.53%) ABOVE TREND leads weekly momentum, followed by PGSUS (1W: +19.89% | 1M: +8.04%) ABOVE TREND and THYAO (1W: +18.77% | 1M: +9.06%) ABOVE TREND. GARAN (1W: +18.41% | 1M: +19.14%) ABOVE TREND adds confirmation from banking.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking & Finance is strong, up 11.60% for the week and 6.16% over one month. GARAN (1W: +18.41% | 1M: +19.14%) ABOVE TREND leads; AKBNK (1W: +12.09% | 1M: +4.11%) ABOVE TREND and ISCTR (1W: +11.20% | 1M: +7.11%) ABOVE TREND also confirm the advance.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry gained 7.14% on the week but remains down 10.67% over one month, leaving the move broad but still recovery-led. FROTO (1W: +11.45% | 1M: +0.07%) ABOVE TREND, EREGL (1W: +9.13% | 1M: -10.49%) RECOVERY, and ASELS (1W: -1.31% | 1M: -3.15%) BELOW TREND show mixed underlying momentum.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
The sector rose 8.38% on the week but remains down 12.57% over one month. TRALT (1W: +17.87% | 1M: -4.73%) RECOVERY and SASA (1W: +10.14% | 1M: -13.30%) RECOVERY are rebounding, while TUPRS (1W: -1.41% | 1M: -15.30%) BELOW TREND remains weak.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Maintain a moderate risk-on stance, favoring leaders in transportation and banking while avoiding indiscriminate exposure to the broad rebound. Keep position sizing disciplined: normal volatility at 32.9% is supportive, but several sectors remain negative over one month.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
Track whether KONTR (1W: +32.84% | 1M: +31.53%) ABOVE TREND and GARAN (1W: +18.41% | 1M: +19.14%) ABOVE TREND sustain leadership, and whether PGSUS (1W: +19.89% | 1M: +8.04%) ABOVE TREND extends its advance. Watch TUPRS (1W: -1.41% | 1M: -15.30%) BELOW TREND for stabilization or renewed weakness.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Transportation and Banking & Finance are the strongest confirmed leaders, with positive weekly and monthly sector returns. Monitor Energy & Chemicals for follow-through after its weekly rebound, given its still-negative 1M return.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
Specific XU100 support and resistance levels were not provided, so no numeric levels can be stated reliably. Watch for breadth to narrow from 8/8 positive or annualized volatility to move above 40%—either would weaken the current risk-on signal.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Normal volatility and 8/8 positive sector breadth support a RISK-ON stance, led by transportation, technology and banking. The main risk is that many sectors remain negative over one month, leaving the broad rally vulnerable if weekly momentum fades.
